title: Gate CSV rerun source overwrite
summary: CSV rerun replace-final can overwrite the CSV source path only when confirm_source_overwrite is explicitly true and backend planning proves the final output resolves to that same path.
reason: A replace-final rerun can intentionally target the original source file when the configured final output root maps back to the source location. The operator requested that overwrite path, so it must be explicit across WebView, API, Python launch policy, PowerShell planning, and pending-publish trust evidence rather than silent or broadly source-root writable.
behavior_before: CSV rerun rejected row-level source mutation aliases, but replace-final destination planning did not have a dedicated confirmation for final_output_path equal to source_path, and pending-publish trust treated source-root destinations as unsafe.
behavior_after: CSV rerun blocks direct publish_replace_final and pending_publish/replace_final rows when final_output_path equals source_path unless confirm_source_overwrite is true. Confirmed rows carry manifest evidence, pending drain trusts only server_out equal to source_path, and sidecars are limited to the confirmed target directory.
tests_added: Extended PowerShell rerun PlanOnly coverage for unconfirmed block and confirmed direct/pending source-path overwrite allow.
Extended Python/WebView policy, launch-plan, API contract, and request-building tests for confirm_source_overwrite.
Extended pending-publish safety checks for confirmed same-path source overwrite and sidecar trust.
